title: Jam Roly-Poly
subtitle: Suet pastry rolled with jam, steamed until tender
excerpt: A suet-pastry sheet spread with raspberry jam, rolled up, wrapped in foil, and steamed until soft and pudding-like. It is one of the most comforting of the old British steamed puddings.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (1861) and Hartley's Modern British Cooking both give the suet-and-flour pastry. The dish is traditionally called 'dead man's arm' in school-dinner culture, a name that refers to its rolled shape.

content.text: Jam roly-poly is a suet-pastry sheet, spread with jam, rolled up and steamed in a foil parcel. The pastry is tender and slightly dense, the jam runs through it in a sticky, sweet seam, and the whole thing steams for 1 hour 45 minutes until thoroughly cooked through. The suet keeps the pastry light during steaming, it does not become heavy the way a butter pastry would.

Combine the flour, suet, and sugar in a large bowl. Add the milk a little at a time, mixing with a fork until the dough just comes together into a soft but not sticky ball. Do not overwork it, stir until combined and stop. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface.

Roll the dough out gently to a rectangle roughly 25cm by 35cm. Spread the jam over the surface, leaving a 2cm border on all sides, this border prevents the jam from squeezing out when you roll and seal the ends. Roll up from the short end, working slowly to keep the roll even. Press the seam and both ends to seal.

Tear off a large piece of foil and a piece of baking paper the same size. Lay the paper on the foil. Butter the paper lightly. Place the roly-poly on top, seam-side down. Fold the paper and foil loosely around it, allow room for the pudding to expand, and crimp the edges to seal. Lower the parcel into a large pan with a tight-fitting lid. Add boiling water to come about 3cm up the sides of the parcel. Cover the pan and steam over a medium-low heat for 1 hour 45 minutes, topping up the water as needed. The water should always be gently simmering, not boiling hard.
Lift the parcel carefully from the pan and rest for 2 minutes before unwrapping. Transfer to a warm serving plate, slice thickly, and serve with custard or cream.

items.symptom: The pastry splits when I roll it up
items.cause: The dough is a little dry, or it was rolled too thin in places.
items.fix: Roll gently and evenly. Patch any tears with a pinch of dough pressed firmly. The foil parcel holds it together during steaming, so small cracks are not critical.

items.symptom: Jam leaks out of the parcel
items.cause: The jam was spread too close to the edge before rolling.
items.fix: Leave a larger border next time. If it has leaked, the jam will simply caramelise against the foil, the pudding inside is still fine.

items.symptom: The centre is still doughy after the full time
items.cause: The water went off the boil during steaming, or the parcel was sealed too tightly.
items.fix: Return to the pan and steam for a further 20 to 30 minutes. Check the water is at a steady simmer throughout.

content.text: Best eaten immediately, straight from the parcel. Leftovers keep for 1 day, wrapped, at room temperature. Reheat by returning to a covered pan of simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes until hot through.
